forecast_convention: Day-ahead: every hour of day D is predicted from information available at 09:00 IST on day D-1. Weather inputs are archived day-ahead forecasts, never observations.

hot_period.definition: Research-defined: population-weighted national daily maximum day-ahead forecast temperature >= 37.67 C (the p90% of daily maxima over the training period). NOT an India Meteorological Department heatwave declaration.

evening_ramp_definition: Research residual load = metered all-India demand (NLDC_DEMAND|P) minus SCADA all-India solar (clipped at 0) and wind. Not an operator net-load definition; excludes behind-the-meter solar, interchange and storage.

extrapolation.note: A gradient-boosted tree predicts a weighted average of training leaf values, so a level-target model cannot exceed the maximum demand it saw in training. The delta-target model predicts the change from the previous day's same hour and adds that anchor back, so it follows load growth beyond the training range.

source_sampling: The Mendeley dataset title claims a 1-hour interval. It is not hourly: the workbooks are 5-minute (r=300) for the earlier months and 10-second (r=10) for the later ones. This pipeline aggregates both regimes to true hourly means.

sources.name: Grid-India / NERLDC SCADA demand and generation
sources.note: Published as '1-hour interval'; the files are actually 5-minute and 10-second SCADA exports. This project aggregates them to true hourly means.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Previous Runs API (archived day-ahead forecasts)
sources.note: Only temperature_2m is archived at a day-ahead lead for 2021-2023, so it is the only weather input the model uses.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (observed)
sources.note: Retrospective analysis only; never a model input.

limitations: Only forecast temperature is available at a genuine day-ahead lead from the archived-forecast source; humidity, radiation, cloud cover and wind forecasts are not, so they are excluded rather than replaced with observations.
The national weather index is population-weighted across 18 load centres. Population is a proxy for, not a measurement of, each region's share of electricity demand.
Hot periods are research-defined by a temperature percentile. They are not India Meteorological Department heatwave declarations.
Residual load is metered demand minus SCADA solar and wind. It excludes behind-the-meter rooftop solar, interchange and storage, so it indicates the evening ramp rather than an operator net load.
Relationships shown between temperature and demand are predictive associations, not causal estimates.
The P10-P90 interval is under-dispersed on the test period and should not be read as a calibrated operational risk band.
The dataset ends on 31 December 2023. Nothing here is live, and no 2024-2026 demand record has been evaluated.
